competencies.text: Explain nervous + endocrine coordination for temperature regulation.
Explain how vaccines work via immune and lymphatic systems.
Describe how damaged parts affect organisms (torn ACL, asthma attack).

days.title: Organ Systems Coordinating
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe how the nervous and endocrine systems coordinate to regulate body temperature (homeostasis), explain how vaccines activate the immune and lymphatic systems, and describe how damage to specific organs affects the whole organism.

🫀 The Human Body as a System of Systems

The human body has 11 major organ systems, all working together:

SystemMain Function
CirculatoryTransports blood, oxygen, nutrients, wastes
RespiratoryGas exchange — O₂ in, CO₂ out
DigestiveBreaks down food, absorbs nutrients
NervousDetects stimuli, sends signals, coordinates responses
EndocrineReleases hormones for long-term regulation
Immune & LymphaticDefends against pathogens; returns fluid to blood
Muscular & SkeletalMovement, support, protection
ExcretoryRemoves waste (urine, sweat)
IntegumentarySkin — protection, temperature regulation
ReproductiveProduces offspring
UrinaryFilters blood, produces urine

🌡️ Coordinating Body Temperature (Homeostasis)

Your body maintains ~37°C. When it changes, the hypothalamus (in the brain) detects the change and coordinates a response through BOTH the nervous and endocrine systems:

StimulusNervous ResponseEndocrine ResponseResult
Too hotSweat glands activated; blood vessels dilate (vasodilation)Thyroid reduces metabolic rateBody cools down
Too coldMuscles shiver; blood vessels constrict (vasoconstriction); hair stands upAdrenaline and thyroid hormones increase heat productionBody warms up

Key idea: The nervous system responds fast (milliseconds) — the endocrine system responds slower but longer-lasting (seconds to hours).

🛡️ The Immune & Lymphatic Systems

Your body has three lines of defense against pathogens:

LineComponentsExample
1st line (barriers)Skin, mucous membranes, tears, stomach acidSkin blocks bacteria; acid kills swallowed pathogens
2nd line (innate)Phagocytes, inflammation, feverWhite blood cells engulf bacteria at a wound
3rd line (adaptive)B cells, T cells, antibodies, memory cellsTargeted attack after exposure to a specific pathogen

Lymphatic system: A network of vessels, lymph nodes, spleen, and thymus that:

  • Returns excess fluid to the blood
  • Filters out pathogens and debris
  • Houses white blood cells that fight infection

💉 How Vaccines Work

  1. Exposure: Vaccine introduces a weakened, inactivated, or partial pathogen (antigen).
  2. Recognition: B cells and T cells recognize the antigen as foreign.
  3. Response: B cells produce antibodies; T cells coordinate the attack.
  4. Memory: Some B and T cells become memory cells that remain in the body.
  5. Future protection: If the real pathogen attacks later, memory cells launch a fast, strong response — often preventing illness entirely.

Vaccines don't give you the disease — they give your immune system a rehearsal.

🦴 When Parts Are Damaged — Case Studies

Injury / ConditionWhat's DamagedEffect on the Organism
Torn ACLAnterior cruciate ligament in the kneeKnee becomes unstable; walking, running, and pivoting become painful/difficult; may need surgery
Asthma attackBronchioles in the lungs constrictAirways narrow; breathing becomes difficult; wheezing; requires inhaler (bronchodilator)
Heart attackHeart muscle loses blood supply (blocked artery)Heart muscle dies; pumping weakens; can be fatal if untreated
StrokeBrain tissue loses blood supplyParalysis, speech loss, memory problems — depends on affected brain area

🌍 Real-Life Applications

  • DepEd immunization programs: Measles, polio, hepatitis B, and tetanus vaccines protect millions of Filipino children.
  • Athlete injury management: ACL injuries require physical therapy and sometimes surgery.
  • Asthma awareness: Inhalers and avoiding triggers (dust, smoke, pollen) are key.
  • Fever: A sign that the immune system is fighting infection — not always a bad thing.

📌 Quick Check

  • Which organ coordinates body temperature? (Answer: hypothalamus)
  • What are the three lines of immune defense? (Answer: barriers, innate, adaptive)
  • How do vaccines protect us? (Answer: by creating memory cells via a safe rehearsal)

days.title: Match Game — Body Systems
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each body system or concept to its correct function. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Brain region that coordinates body temperature
Blood vessels widen to release heat when you're hot
Blood vessels narrow to keep heat when you're cold
Skin, mucous membranes, tears, stomach acid
B and T cells that remain after infection to fight future attacks
A weakened pathogen used to train the immune system safely
Damaged knee ligament — causes instability during movement
Bronchioles in the lungs constrict, making breathing difficult

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Immunity & Injury
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🥵 You run a race under the hot sun and start sweating heavily. Which two systems are coordinating to cool you down?

choices.label: A) Only the nervous system
B) The nervous system (sweat glands) and the endocrine system (hormones regulating metabolism)
C) Only the endocrine system
D) The digestive and respiratory systems

scenario.text: 💉 A child receives the measles vaccine. A few weeks later, they are exposed to a real measles virus but do not get sick. Why?

choices.label: A) The vaccine gave them the disease
B) Memory B and T cells recognized the virus and produced antibodies quickly, stopping the infection
C) The virus can't infect children
D) It was just luck

scenario.text: 🦵 A basketball player lands badly and tears their ACL. What is a likely consequence?

choices.label: A) The knee becomes unstable; running, jumping, and pivoting become painful or impossible
B) The player loses the ability to breathe
C) Their vision is affected
D) Nothing — the ACL is not important

scenario.text: 🌬️ A student has an asthma attack during PE class. What is happening in their body?

choices.label: A) Their heart has stopped
B) The bronchioles in their lungs constricted, narrowing the airways and making breathing hard
C) They have a broken rib
D) They have a fever

scenario.text: 🩹 You get a small cut on your finger and it becomes red, warm, and slightly swollen. What is happening?

choices.label: A) You are having an allergic reaction
B) Your 2nd line of defense — inflammation — is sending white blood cells to fight any pathogens that entered
C) The cut is infected and untreatable
D) Your immune system is failing

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Anatomy Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Anatomy Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: Which brain region coordinates body temperature?

choices.label: A) Hypothalamus
B) Cerebellum
C) Brain stem
D) Frontal lobe

escape.text: What is the 1st line of defense against pathogens?

choices.label: A) Physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes
B) Antibodies
C) Memory cells
D) Vaccines

escape.text: How do vaccines protect you from future infections?

choices.label: A) They create memory B and T cells that respond quickly if the real pathogen appears
B) They kill all pathogens in your body permanently
C) They replace your immune system
D) They cause the disease in a mild form only

escape.text: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between nervous and endocrine responses?

choices.label: A) Nervous is fast and short-term; endocrine is slower but longer-lasting
B) Nervous is slow; endocrine is fast
C) They are identical
D) Only nervous responses involve hormones

escape.text: A torn ACL affects which body part?

choices.label: A) The knee joint
B) The heart
C) The lungs
D) The brain

escape.text: Which of the following is a symptom of an asthma attack?

choices.label: A) Difficulty breathing and wheezing due to narrowed bronchioles
B) Broken bones
C) Rapid hair growth
D) Loss of vision
